name: ui-layouts-carousel
title: Carousel
description: A horizontal image carousel with translucent round arrow buttons, a current-slide counter and dash-style dots. Slides glide sideways and wrap around at the ends.
use: A page needs to show a handful of photos one at a time with simple controls.
avoid: Controls are fixed-size and the slide height is set in the demo, so tall art needs resizing.
a11y: Arrow buttons have no accessible names and the root hides its focus outline. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A wide rounded photo slide, a white hillside town, with translucent circular arrow buttons at mid-left and mid-right. Below it a small mono counter reads 1 / 4 on the left and four short dash dots sit at the right.
behaves: Clicking an arrow or dot slides the photo horizontally to the next frame with a short ease; the counter and the dark active dash update, and arrows dim at the ends. Arrow keys also page it.
customise: options and plugins drive the slider; slides, arrows, counter and dots are separate child components you compose and style.
weight: light: Four images with embla drag plus small counter animation; no canvas or loop.
demo: Santorini rooftops, a wooden deck and a seaside telescope
issues: Arrow buttons show only icons, with no labels for screen readers.
The slide counter is tiny mono text that is easy to miss.
polishWhy: Clean rounded slider with tidy controls; default arrows and a tiny counter keep it standard.
